Abstract:

India&rsquos semiconductor industry is gaining national importance, creating an increasing demand for skilled professionals. The Semicon India Future Skills Talent Committee Report projects a requirement of approximately 1.2 million semiconductor-related professionals by 2032. Meeting this demand requires practical training in critical fabrication processes, particularly lithography, where precision in pattern formation, equipment handling, and process control is essential. However, the high cost of commercial equipment, limited access to industrial facilities, and risks associated with improper operation restrict hands-on training opportunities.

This research proposes an Augmented Reality (AR)-based immersive safety training environment for laser lithography systems through three objectives. First, it will develop an interactive virtual representation of the equipment, incorporating major components, structured training pathways, Causal Loop Diagrams (CLDs), and audio cues to support equipment familiarisation and procedural learning. Second, it will examine how trainees develop mental models by assessing their understanding of potential hazards, equipment conditions, operational relationships, and appropriate safety responses. Third, it will formulate a safety training framework and AR-based design interventions informed by identified learning gaps and critical failure events established through Z-SAM-based Fault Tree Analysis. The interventions will include interactive demonstrations, hazard visualisation, contextual safety instructions, and scenario-based activities.
